originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches against published mathematical records and full-text comparisons found no statement of the complete all-element left Hopf-adjoint rank polynomial for the four-dimensional Sweedler algebra. The primary 2026 paper treats a different invariant; the earlier full-text cohomology paper employs the adjoint module but does not state the enumerator. The same-algebra ordinary polynomial identity equivalence with UT2 does not imply the kernel or rank fibers of the Hopf adjoint representation. A historically unindexed decomposition is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Older representation-theoretic treatments may explicitly decompose the Sweedler adjoint module without using the word rank; a decomposition could dominate the structural part and imply the rank polynomial.
Full-text comparisons were limited to identified likely sources; older specialist treatments using different module terminology could still imply the full rank polynomial.
The result is intentionally small-dimensional; its value depends on the naturalness of this canonical first Hopf example, not a claimed general breakthrough.

value.rationale: The full rank census and forbidden rank-three stratum provide a natural quantitative invariant for the canonical finite-dimensional noncommutative and noncocommutative Hopf algebra. The triangular quotient and indecomposable action block give the mechanism and make it a reproducible benchmark relevant to adjoint-module cohomology and operator stratification. The result is bounded to this example, with no claimed general theory.
